work_order.root_cause: Two distinct causes, one per class of finding. (1) The bad-code sweep added by #68 exercises three routes against a fixture, usdRepos('ZZZ'), that creates a tenant and one opportunity and no experiments - so on /experiments the page renders its empty state and every assertion in the loop is true vacuously. The property the test claims to hold ('a call site the change moved that nobody enumerated') is untested on the one route whose call sites (#68 moved tenantCurrency() into experimentCard's two cards.map sites) the change actually added. (2) Four doc comments written in #68 assert a stronger guarantee than the code gives: a bad code is said to match 'no stored spend row' and exclude a bad row's amounts from the funnel, but computeFunnel treats a spend row whose payload carries NO currency as tenant-currency (src/domain/measurement.js:203, `if (currency !== undefined && currency !== tenantCurrency) continue`), and that shape is reachable through the live ingest path because normaliseGrowthEvent validates payload.currency only when it is present (src/domain/measurement.js:136). The behaviour is pre-existing and identical on main - this is a documentation defect, not a regression.
work_order.understanding: Issue #72 bundles six non-blocking review findings left by #68 / PR #70. I reproduced all six on the current default branch (8e9ef8c) before planning. F1 REPRODUCES: the new sweep at test/web/pages.test.js:1224 is vacuous on /experiments. Its fixture usdRepos() (pages.test.js:59-73) creates a tenant and one opportunity and no experiment, so /experiments renders its empty state and all four loop assertions are true of nothing. I mutated experimentCard's `Max spend ${escapeHtml(money(caps.max_spend_micros, currency))}` to `${escapeHtml(String(caps.max_spend_micros))}` and the suite read 63 pass / 0 fail - the sweep detects nothing. The four pre-existing tests that do catch it (38, 45, 56, 57) all fixture a healthy USD/INR tenant. I then built the proposed fix and re-ran the same mutation: 59 pass / 5 fail, with the sweep (53) now among the red. F2 REPRODUCES: src/api/routes.js:65 says a bad code is passed through VERBATIM 'so it matches no stored spend row', and src/web/pages.js:211 says the same code is passed through 'so a bad row's amounts are excluded from the dashboard funnel too'. Neither is true. src/domain/measurement.js:203 skips a spend row only when `currency !== undefined && currency !== tenantCurrency`, so a row carrying no currency is summed and a CPL is drawn from it; and such a row is reachable live, since normaliseGrowthEvent only validates payload.currency when present (src/domain/measurement.js:136). I confirmed the two comment instances and the code they overstate. F3 PARTIALLY ACTIONABLE: the ask is a note in PR #70's description, but PR #70 merged at 2026-09-26T01:58:35Z - there is no pre-merge reader left to serve, and this ticket opens a new PR. The substance is real and durable, so I fold it into the routes.js comment this ticket already rewrites: the reversal of #66's pin and the operator-visible consequence (an already-bad row now reads 0 spend and a null CPL) belong next to the read that produces them, permanently. F4 REPRODUCES: the same overstatement as F2 at src/web/pages.js:211, the copy a dashboard reader hits first. F5 REPRODUCES: src/web/pages.js:251 says 'every money() call on every screen for such a tenant arrives here with an unknown code'. money() tests isReadableComponent before the ISO_CURRENCIES membership test (pages.js:266-270), so the funnel tile at 438 for a bad-code tenant returns the em-dash at the readability guard and never evaluates membership - and /journal and /approvals draw no money at all. I also measured the companion claim: replacing the fallback with a bare `currency` turns 4 tests red in test/web/pages.test.js (15, 52, 53, 55), not 8. The code comment states no number, so the 4-vs-8 correction lands in the comment as a measured figure rather than as a fix to a wrong number. F6 DOES NOT NEED WORK: the reviewer's own fix says the file-local helper convention is defensible and 'Do not do it inside this PR on its own merits'. I decline it in out_of_scope rather than implement a change the finding declines.

AC-2 is satisfied only at the doc comment it names (lines 63-93, above resolveTenantCurrency). The SAME overstatement survives verbatim 140 lines below, on the call site that actually produces the number: the inline comment above `const tenantCurrency = resolveTenantCurrency(...)` in the GET /v1/metrics handler still reads "A stored code naming no ISO currency is used verbatim, so it matches no spend row". That is the exact sentence AC-2 was chartered to retire, and it is still false for the same reason measurement.js:203 gives: computeFunnel skips a spend row only when `currency !== undefined && currency !== tenantCurrency`, so a spend row carrying NO currency IS summed. A reader who lands on the route (the natural place to check what the API returns) gets the un-narrowed claim, and now gets it in a file whose other comment explicitly says the opposite — the two comments in this one file now contradict each other. AC-2's own invariant ('the comment's guarantee holds for every spend row that names a currency, and it names the one class of row for which it does not') is met at 66 and unmet at 231.

`src/api/routes.js:231`

Evidence: `sed -n '229,233p' src/api/routes.js` on branch sdlc/issue-72 prints the comment unchanged: '// legacy batches may still hold. A stored code naming no ISO currency is / // used verbatim, so it matches no spend row; INR applies only when the / // tenant has no row at all.' `git diff main..HEAD -- src/api/routes.js | grep -c "matches no spend row"` returns 0 — the PR never touched it. The claim is false: src/domain/measurement.js:203 is `if (currency !== undefined && currency !== tenantCurrency) { continue; }`, so a payload with no currency is summed. grep confirms this is the only surviving instance: `grep -rn "matches no" src/` returns exactly two hits, routes.js:66 (narrowed by this PR) and routes.js:231 (not narrowed).

Fix: Narrow the call-site comment to match line 66's wording — 'so it matches no spend row THAT CARRIES A CURRENCY' — and add the same one-clause exception the doc comment now carries, pointing at src/domain/measurement.js:203. Comment-only; no code change. Alternatively, delete the call-site comment and let it defer to the resolveTenantCurrency doc comment it is restating, so there is one place to keep true.

review.title: The new assertion extracts its subject with `page.match(/data-testid="caps">[^<]*/)[0]`. When the caps span is absent the regex returns null and `[0]` throws a TypeError before assert.equal ever runs, so the test fails with 'Cannot read properties of null (reading 0)' — an error naming neither the route, the branch, nor the expected string. The assertion message that would have diagnosed it is unreachable in exactly the case it was written for. The test does still fail (so this is not a vacuity defect), but a mutation that removes a branch now produces a message that reads like a harness bug rather than a currency regression.

`test/web/pages.test.js:1272`

Evidence: Breaking only the ideal branch (903 -> literal 'NO-CARDS', so the partial branch still renders a card) yields: `not ok 53 ... error: "Cannot read properties of null (reading '0')"` — the assert.equal message ('the card's caps render relabelled on /experiments') never appears. The same null-guard gap applies per-branch, so the failure never says which of the two branches lost its card.

Fix: Assert the match exists before indexing it, so the branch name survives: `const caps = page.match(...); assert.ok(caps, 'the card's caps render on /experiments' + branch); assert.equal(caps[0], ...)`. Or use assert.match(page, /data-testid="caps">Max spend ₹500\.00 · max downside ₹200\.00/) with the branch name in the message, which needs no index at all.

review.title: The new comment says that under the bare fixture '/experiments drew its empty state and all four assertions held of nothing'. There are three assertions in that loop, not four. Counting the loop body: `assert.doesNotMatch(html, /ZZZ/...)`, `assert.doesNotMatch(html, /NaN|undefined/...)`, and `assert.doesNotMatch(text, /\d{7,}/...)` — three, and the `const text = ...` between them is a derivation, not an assertion. This is the exact defect class the ticket exists to retire: a comment asserting a countable fact about the code that is false. The companion countable claim the PR adds to src/web/pages.js is correct — I measured it (removing the INR fallback at pages.js:276 reds exactly tests 15, 52, 53, 55, the four the comment names), so the PR gets one count right and one wrong.

review.title: The final paragraph of resolveTenantCurrency's doc comment is a six-line changelog narrating the relationship between issue #66, its QA run, PR #70 and issue #68, carrying two concrete figures (7_200_000_000 spend, a ₹2,400.00 tile) that describe a baseline this codebase DELIBERATELY REVERSED. That is the wrong kind of content for this comment and the wrong place for it. The rest of src/ uses issue references as one-clause provenance tags — `issue #22` at pages.js:472, repositories.js:559, routes.js:401, `issue #21` at db.js:164 — never as a narrative with numbers. The 3am test: a reader paged to resolveTenantCurrency who has not read issues #66 and #68 and PR #70 cannot use this paragraph, and the figures are actively hazardous to skim, because 'a ZZZ tenant reading 7_200_000_000 spend' reads as a statement about current behaviour when it is a statement about behaviour that was removed. The behaviour claim itself is correct — I checked it, and a bad code does read 0 spend and null CPL, since computeFunnel returns `qualified_cpl_micros: volume > 0 && spend > 0 ? ... : null` (src/domain/measurement.js:217) and spend is 0 when every currency-carrying row is skipped. It is only the placement and the stale numbers that are wrong. The work order's justification — that PR #70's description was the alternative and is closed — does not hold, because the durable record the paragraph claims to be is already git history, and the review trail is on the PR.
